proposition: Everything a man needs to get himself home — tools, food, and the one photograph — goes into a single 30L Mokobara Transit Backpack, and still goes on his back.

board.style_line: Photoreal cinematic vertical 9:16 frame, handheld weight without shake, 35mm-equivalent lens, one hard low sun as the single fictional source coming from the sea side of frame right; cold desaturated island palette of grey-black wet sand, grey-green sea and bleached driftwood, graded down so exactly one saturated element exists in the frame — the bright yellow lining of the backpack; deep shadow detail held, no crushed blacks, no lens flare, no slow motion.
board.negative_line: no text, no logos, no letterforms, no numbers, no signage, no subtitles, no watermark, no brand marks on any surface, no second bag, no modern vehicles or buildings, no crowds, no other people, no cartoon or impossible-scale exaggeration, no gore, no slow motion, no rack focus.

identity_anchors.front: vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls
identity_anchors.harness: black padded straps, small top grab handle

hero_frame.description: The backpack stands open and dead centre on wet grey sand, its mouth spread toward camera so the bright yellow lining is lit from inside by the low sun, and running away from that mouth toward the water at frame right lies one straight line of everything that came out of it: a coil of rope, a lashed wooden spear, a folded tarp, a dented tin, two dozen small fish wrapped in leaves, four coconuts. The man sits at frame left at the head of the line, one hand still inside the pack. The line of objects is longer than he is.

audio.music_bed: Native location sound is the spine: distant surf, wind over sand, and close dry handling noise — sand dragged off nylon, the zip, rope, water at the shins. Music is one low sustained string-and-breath bed, no melody, no percussion, no jingle: it enters at 12.5 s under the fifth object coming out of the pack, after the picture has already made the delight, lifts slightly at 19.5 s as he packs, resolves on his second step into the water at 25.5 s and ends one second before the last frame. The first seven seconds carry no music at all, so the opening sound promises nothing the film does not keep.

beats.title: The tide gives it back
beats.feeling: A jolt of wrong-thing-here — recognition arriving before understanding: that is a made object, a modern one, and it has been under this sand a long time.
beats.framing: Extreme close-up, camera set low and level with the sand, sea a soft grey band out of focus at frame right. Centre-left, a weathered hand drags back a fan of wet black sand. Under it a black padded strap and the small top grab handle of the deep navy matte body surface, still half buried; seawater fills the drag marks and runs back in. Nothing else is in frame but sand, the hand, and the strap. Camera static; the only movement in frame is the hand and the water.
beats.first_frame: Wet black sand filling the whole vertical frame. A single black padded strap and the small top grab handle break the surface off-centre, low-left, one hard low-sun highlight running along the strap's edge and a rim of sand grains on the webbing. The hand has not yet entered frame.
beats.impact: Static camera, one continuous take, no cut inside it. The hand enters from frame left on the second beat of the surf. Sound does the work the picture cannot: far surf and wind, then the close, dry scrape of sand on nylon — reality established by ear before the eye has named the object. Hold four seconds after the grab handle clears, long enough to read it. No music.

beats.title: One pull of the zip
beats.feeling: Relief with a catch in it — the thing survived, and so, therefore, might he.
beats.framing: Tight three-quarter, camera at chest height. The pack now stands upright between his knees, deep navy matte body filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, sand still packed into its seams. His hand takes the lower of the two black zip pulls on the front bucket pocket, then the upper one on the vertical front zip, and draws it the full length of the body. The bright yellow lining opens as a hard wedge of colour — the single saturated thing in a frame of cold grey sand, grey sea and bleached driftwood. Sea stays frame right.
beats.first_frame: The closed pack upright, three-quarter to camera, salt-dried and sand-crusted; both black zip pulls hanging dead straight at the foot of the vertical front zip; his two hands at the frame's lower edge with fingers on the pulls, not yet moving; the bucket pocket's shape reading clearly against the flat sea behind.
beats.impact: The camera holds still on purpose; the zip is the only move, so nothing competes with it. One take, so the yellow arrives as an event rather than as a shot change. The zip is mixed closest and driest of anything in the film so far, against far surf. The supplied wordmark composites into the upper third at 7.0 s while the zip is still travelling, so the name lands inside ten seconds without stealing the reveal.

beats.title: What was in it
beats.feeling: Delight, then a small disbelief that stays on the right side of possible: the laugh is at the quantity, never at the man.
beats.framing: Wide, camera on the sand, subject centred because the scene points inward — the open pack sits dead centre, mouth spread toward camera, yellow lining lit from inside by the low sun. Running away from that mouth toward the water at frame right, one straight line of contents: coil of rope, lashed wooden spear, folded tarp, dented tin, two dozen small fish wrapped in leaves, four coconuts. The man sits at frame left at the head of the line, one hand still inside the pack, finding one more thing. The line is longer than he is; he is the scale figure.
beats.first_frame: The pack centred and open, yellow mouth to camera, the line of objects already laid out and completely still, the two nearest coconuts closest to the water at frame right; the man's hand inside the pack to the wrist, his face down; no motion anywhere in the frame.
beats.impact: Static wide, no camera move at all — blocking alone directs the eye: pack, then down the line, then back to the man. The spear, the late-found third element in the line, is sized to stay findable at phone delivery size. The laugh is held rather than cut: the shot runs its full describe-aloud length, the longest hold in the film. Music enters at 12.5 s under the fifth object, channelling delight the picture has already made. '30L' composites into the upper third at 11.5 s, opposed to the pack at the other end of the long axis.

beats.title: The photograph
beats.feeling: The turn — the joke stops and you understand why he was counting fish.
beats.framing: Tight two-shot staged in depth: his face at frame left, three-quarters to camera and in focus, lit by the same low sun; in his raised hand at frame right, held up into that light, a small sun-bleached photograph of a woman, her face soft but readable. The cold grey sea sits a stop down behind both. The front bucket pocket hangs open and empty at the bottom of frame, the two black zip pulls swinging.
beats.first_frame: His hand lifting the photograph clear of the bright yellow lining, the photo's white border catching the low sun; his face behind and left of it still turned down toward the pack, not yet up; the yellow lining a narrow bar of colour along the frame's lower edge.
beats.impact: The eye plays between the two faces — he comes up into the light, the photograph stays still, the dominant living face brings the eye back — so the shot is active without a camera move. He then looks off frame left toward the open sea, a look the next beat pays off from a matching height and angle. Surf drops a level; the music holds one note and does not swell. Cut out on the look, which motivates the departure.

beats.title: Packing to go
beats.feeling: Purpose — the fast, tidy competence of someone who has just decided.
beats.framing: Medium, camera slightly high. The pack lies on its back on the sand, bright yellow lining up and facing camera, deep navy matte body dark against the pale dry sand. His hands load it in one continuous pass: tarp flat to the back panel, fish and coconuts down the centre, tin and rope to the sides, the lashed wooden spear run along the outside of the body under the straps, and the photograph last, sliding into the front bucket pocket, both black zip pulls drawn shut over it. Sea stays frame right; direction of travel unchanged.
beats.first_frame: The empty pack lying open on the sand, the yellow lining a clean rectangle of colour at frame centre; the line of objects from the previous beat now gathered in a heap at the frame's right edge; his two hands just entering at the top of frame, empty.
beats.impact: One camera move only — a slow ten-percent push in as the last item goes in, hidden behind the hands' action and lit for both ends of the move, so the technique is not noticed. The sound is the labour: nylon, the double zip, rope on wood, sand. Music lifts underneath without taking over. The beat ends holding on the closed front bucket pocket, so the photograph's place is the last thing seen before he stands.

beats.title: On his back, into the water
beats.feeling: Weight lifting — the plain physical satisfaction of a load that sits exactly where it should.
beats.framing: Low wide from behind and slightly below, the low sun and the sea ahead of him at frame right. He swings the pack up; the black padded straps settle onto his shoulders, the small top grab handle stands proud, the deep navy matte body reads as the flattest, darkest shape against the glare on the water. He walks left to right into the shallows toward a lashed raft, water to his shins. He does not look back.
beats.first_frame: The pack at the end of one arm mid-swing, halfway to his shoulder, his back to camera; the sun a hard low disc on the water at frame right; his far foot already turned toward the sea; the yellow lining just visible as a thread at the closed zip line.
beats.impact: Camera static; his movement across the frame is the motion, and the pack is the highest-contrast shape travelling through it, so nothing needs to be pointed at. Surf comes up in level as he enters the water; the music resolves on his second step. Cut on the third step, at the top of a wave, through two frames of black into the close.

beats.title: The pack, and where to get one
beats.feeling: Quiet recognition — that is the bag you just watched do all of it.
beats.framing: Code-composed brand close, no generated motion. The product sits three-quarter to camera on clean wet sand in the same first light, at the angle showing the most surfaces — front face, one side and the top together — so the vertical front zip, the front bucket pocket and both black zip pulls all read, with one black padded strap fallen forward to show its padding and the small top grab handle upright. Pack in the lower two-thirds; the supplied wordmark and the composited lines in the upper third, opposed at the far end of the long axis, over the plain out-of-focus sea.
beats.first_frame: The pack alone on the wet sand, sea soft behind it, no type yet: the first composited frame brings the supplied wordmark and the three lines up together in one step.
beats.impact: No motion at all — a deliberate stillness after six beats of hands and water. Two-frame dissolve out of the previous beat's black, then a flat three-second hold, longer than it takes to read three short lines aloud. Surf continues underneath at the level of the last shot so the place does not end with the picture; the music finishes one second before the last frame, leaving the pack in the sound of the sea.

name_lockup.why: Attribution inside ten seconds, entering while the zip is still travelling so it does not compete with the yellow reveal. Upper-third zone, opposed along the long axis to the pack in the lower two-thirds; the supplied wordmark SVG is placed unaltered immediately above the line, never redrawn or recoloured. Ground under both is the flat out-of-focus grey sea, measured at its lightest and darkest point for at least 4.5:1 against the type colour; mixed case, medium weight, no all-caps, no thin face.

capacity_super.why: Lands on the hero frame, at the moment the line of contents is fully out, so the number reads as the explanation of what the eye has just refused to believe. Same upper-third zone as the name so the two supers never occupy different parts of the frame; sits over cold flat sand, contrast measured at both extremes of that ground at delivery size; large weight, so 3:1 is the floor and 4.5:1 the target.

close_card.why: The close names the product, restates the one specific figure, and makes the single ask. Three lines only, ranked by size: product name largest, 30L beneath it, mokobara.com last and smallest but still above the findable size at phone delivery, all composited as real text over an even, out-of-focus sea ground chosen for uniform luminance so every line measures at least 4.5:1 across its whole box. The supplied wordmark sits above them, untouched.

mandatory.customer_words: lets make an ad with mokobara
mandatory.realisation: The film has one product in it and nothing else to sell: the Mokobara Transit Backpack is on screen in every one of the seven beats, is the object the whole story turns on, and is the last thing seen. The supplied wordmark enters at 7.0 s and again on the close card.

mandatory.customer_words: i would preferably give it the odysey movie angel
mandatory.realisation: The register is the epic homecoming, carried by archetype alone: a man years stranded, a wife's photograph, a raft, a sea crossed to get home. Beat 4 is the emotional hinge that makes it a homecoming rather than a survival clip. No named work, character, line, poster image, casting or costume from any specific film or text is used — see M9.

The pack is established as already his: it is dug out of the sand of the beach he was wrecked on, it carries the photograph he packed before the crossing, and it is salt-dried and sand-crusted in beat 2 — worn, not new, not found abandoned by someone else.

mandatory.customer_words: the protagonist found his mokobara bag, while he was on the island where he was kept for years
mandatory.realisation: Beat 1 is the find itself and is the first frame of the film: a weathered hand drags back wet sand and a black padded strap and the small top grab handle surface. The years are carried by the state of him and of the pack, not by a caption.

mandatory.customer_words: in that bag he founds her wives photo
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4: the sun-bleached photograph of a woman comes out of the yellow lining and is held up into the light beside his face — the only beat with a human face in close-up, and the reason the film stops being funny.

mandatory.customer_words: and a lot of stuff that he could use to go back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 3 lays the whole inventory out in one line running away from the pack's mouth: rope, spear, tarp, tin, fish, coconuts — every item a means of getting off the island, not decoration. Beat 5 puts all of it back in.

mandatory.customer_words: he packs food and stuff and goes back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 5 is the packing, item by item in one continuous pass, food down the centre; beat 6 is the departure — pack shouldered, into the shallows toward the raft, left to right, no look back.

mandatory.customer_words: would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff
mandatory.realisation: The comic beat is beat 3 and it is played straight: a static wide, no cut, no cartoon scaling, the man lying at the head of a line of contents longer than he is. His arms are there as a lashed wooden spear and a dented tin — tools, no firearms — and the food is two dozen fish and four coconuts. The exaggeration rests on a truth the next super states: 30L. The laugh is at the quantity, never at the man.

mandatory.customer_words: Avoid getting copyright violoations from odysssey
mandatory.realisation: Nothing named, quoted or copied: no title, character name, place name, crew, monster, ship design, costume, poster composition or musical motif from any specific film or text. The prompts contain no proper nouns at all, and the negative line bars every letterform inside generated pixels. Only public archetype is used — castaway, photograph, raft — and the one proper name on screen is the brand's own.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings: "Transit Backpack", "30L", "mokobara.com" — placement overlay, script latin, may_reflow false
mandatory.realisation: All three exist only as composited text layers, never generated pixels, never reflowed or re-broken: 'Transit Backpack' at 7.0–11.0 s, '30L' at 11.5–14.5 s, and all three together on the close card at 27.0–30.0 s.

mandatory.customer_words: aspect 9:16, count 1, kind multi_shot_story, modality video, motion from generated, audio true, seconds 30
mandatory.realisation: One film, seven contiguous beats, 0 to 30.000 s, composed vertical throughout with the long axis used deliberately (subject low, type high); every moving beat is a generated still taken to image-to-video and stitched by code; the seventh is code-composed with clip_s 0. Native audio on, no voice-over.

mandatory.customer_words: identity_invariants: deep navy matte body / bright yellow lining / vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls / black padded straps, small top grab handle
mandatory.realisation: All four are restated verbatim as identity anchors in every prompt, and each is given a beat where it is unmistakably legible: grab handle and strap in beat 1, front zip and both pulls in beat 2, lining in beat 3, pulls again closing over the photograph in beat 5, straps and navy body in beat 6, and all four together at the most-surfaces angle on the close.

mandatory.customer_words: reference_assets: mokobara_wordmark (role logo, image/svg+xml) and transit_backpack_private_island_1 (role product, image/jpeg)
mandatory.realisation: The wordmark is composited from the supplied SVG, placed and never redrawn, restyled, recoloured or regenerated, at 7.0 s and on the close card. The supplied product JPEG is the likeness reference for every beat's still, so the generated pack matches the real colourway and hardware rather than a plausible invention.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product itself is on screen from frame one — a black padded strap and the small top grab handle in the sand — and never lapses for a single beat: it is opened at 5 s, is the centre of the hero frame at 9.5–15 s, is loaded at 19.5 s, is worn in use at 24 s and is the last image of the film. The supplied wordmark is composited in at 7.0 s, inside the ten-second window, and again on the close card. Branding is carried by more than one asset type: the product in use, the in-situ hardware details, the composited wordmark and the composited type.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the job's standing constraint bars dialogue and voice-over, so the name is never said; the on-screen channel carries the name and the ask alone, and the film is built to work with the sound off (declared deviation D2).

last_frame: The Transit Backpack alone, three-quarter to camera on clean wet sand in low first light, front zip, front bucket pocket and both black zip pulls reading, one black padded strap fallen forward, small top grab handle upright, the out-of-focus sea behind; the supplied wordmark and the three composited lines held in the upper third, with surf still running under the picture.

deviations.from: / / default and : no humour unless a brief clause asks — set out to be interesting, not funny; Hopkins bans amusement outright.
deviations.brief_clause: "would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff" — the customer asks for the comic beat by name. It is taken as an accent, not a language: one beat of the seven, played with a static camera and a real 30L load, carrying the selling point (capacity) rather than sitting beside it, and surrendered at beat 4 so the film ends on feeling.

deviations.from: / / default: the brand name is spoken as well as shown, and the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words (premise: audio is heard).
deviations.brief_clause: The job's standing constraint — "no dialogue or voice-over" — with deliverable_request.motion.audio true. Native sound and one music bed carry the track; the brand name and the single ask are carried by the on-screen channel alone. The corpus is explicit that it does not cover sound-off feed viewing, so the film is additionally built to pass the muted test.

deviations.from: / / default: every cut carries continuous space and at least 30 degrees of angle change; spatial continuity is preserved.
deviations.brief_clause: deliverable_request.exact_text_strings requires three non-reflowing overlays and the film must close on the product inside 30 s (count 1, seconds 30). The beat 6 to beat 7 cut therefore leaves the location entirely. The sacrifice is taken from the bottom of the list — spatial continuity only — and is bridged by two frames of black, a dissolve of chosen duration, and unbroken surf at the same level across the cut; emotion, story and rhythm are all kept.

deviations.from: / default: flag the buyer or the place by name; feeling attaches to one named individual, not a category.
deviations.brief_clause: The job's standing constraint "no named film, actor, character or copyrighted work", read with the brief's own unnamed "the proatagonist" and with 's ban on an invented person. The individual is therefore made specific by face, hands, the state of his clothes and one photograph rather than by a name, and the only proper name anywhere on screen is the brand's own.
